name: פעולה בינארית מוגדרת – מתי היא חילופית (באנגלית)
questiontext:
If \( {{CT:0}}\circ {{CT:1}} \) is defined to mean {{CT:2}}, what must {{CT:3}} equal for \( {{CT:0}}\circ {{CT:1}} = {{CT:1}}\circ {{CT:0}} \) to be true?

{{CT:3}}=[[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: We know: \[ {{CT:0}}\circ {{CT:1}} = {{CT:4}} \mbox{ and } {{CT:1}}\circ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:5}}. \] So the question asks when are these are equal, that is when does: \[ {{CT:4}}={{CT:5}}. \] Putting similar terms on the same side, and simplifying we get: \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}},\\ {{CT:6}}{{CT:0}}-{{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}}{{CT:1}}-{{CT:1}},\\ {{CT:7}}{{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}}{{CT:1}},\\ {{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:1}}. \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: It seems you have formed your equation wrong. Remember that \(b \circ d\) is different from \(d \circ b\)
